fullName: SSC Multi-Tasking (Non-Technical) Staff and Havaldar in CBIC & CBN Examination (MTS & Havaldar)
overview: SSC MTS & Havaldar is the Staff Selection Commission's **Matriculation-level entry exam for Group C posts** in central government offices. It fills two kinds of jobs: **Multi-Tasking Staff (Non-Technical)** in ministries and departments, and **Havaldar** in the Central Board of Indirect Taxes & Customs (CBIC) and the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN). Class 10 is enough to apply. The written test is a **single computer-based exam split into two sessions** - Session 1 covers numerical ability and reasoning, Session 2 covers general awareness and English - and **both sessions must be cleared separately**. MTS selection ends with the CBT plus document verification; **Havaldar candidates additionally face a Physical Efficiency Test and Physical Standard Test (PET/PST)**. Because Session 1 has no negative marking and Session 2 carries a heavy one (-1 on a +3 question), the winning plan is: attempt everything in Session 1, and be selective but sharp in Session 2.

latestCycle.notes: The headline figure of 7,948 vacancies is the latest total reported for this cycle (6,078 MTS in the 18-25 group, 732 MTS in the 18-27 group and 1,138 Havaldar); the number was revised several times, so treat the official vacancy notice as final. Reported figures: about 36.2 lakh applications and about 8.05 lakh candidates appearing in the CBT. Shortlisting for PET/PST used a 1:7 ratio on normalised Session 2 marks. There is no Tier 2 in this exam.

stages.name: CBT Session 1 - Numerical & Reasoning
stages.notes: Session 1 carries **no negative marking**, so leave nothing blank. You must score the minimum qualifying marks in this session separately; skipping a session means disqualification. Marks are normalised across shifts. Questions come in English, Hindi and 13 regional languages.

stages.name: CBT Session 2 - General Awareness & English
stages.notes: Session 2 has **1 mark negative per wrong answer**. In the 2025-26 cycle the PET/PST shortlist was drawn on normalised Session 2 marks, after candidates cleared both sessions. Tip: attempt questions you are at least 60-70 percent sure of; a blind guess in a negative-marked section costs you more than it earns.

selectionProcess: **CBT (Session 1 + Session 2) -> PET/PST (Havaldar only) -> Document Verification -> Allotment.** Both sessions are compulsory and you must meet the minimum qualifying marks in each. Results are drawn from **normalised** marks, with cut-offs varying by post, category and the collecting authority or region. For the 2025-26 cycle, SSC shortlisted Havaldar candidates for the physical tests at a **1:7 ratio** using Session 2 normalised marks. The PET/PST standards reported for Havaldar are: **men** - walk 1,600 metres in 15 minutes or cycle 8 km in 30 minutes, height 157.5 cm, chest 76 cm (81 cm expanded); **women** - walk 1 km in 20 minutes or cycle 3 km in 25 minutes, height 152 cm. PET/PST is **qualifying only** and marks do not count in merit. MTS has no physical test and no interview.
normalization: Since the CBT runs in many shifts with different question papers, SSC **normalises the marks across shifts** so that a harder paper is not a disadvantage. Practical consequences: (1) your raw score is not your final score - the normalised figure decides the result; (2) never compare raw marks across shifts, days or years; (3) attempt every Session 1 question regardless of how hard your shift feels, because there is no negative marking there; (4) in Session 2, accuracy matters more than volume because each wrong answer costs a mark.

faqs.q: What is the exam pattern of SSC MTS?
faqs.a: One computer-based test in **two sessions of 45 minutes each**. Session 1 has 40 questions (20 numerical and mathematical ability, 20 reasoning and problem solving) for 120 marks. Session 2 has 50 questions (25 general awareness, 25 English) for 150 marks. In total that is **90 questions and 270 marks**.

faqs.q: What is the negative marking in SSC MTS?
faqs.a: **Session 1 has no negative marking.** In **Session 2, each wrong answer costs 1 mark**, while a correct answer earns 3. Unanswered questions score zero in both sessions.

faqs.q: Do I have to qualify in both sessions?
faqs.a: Yes. Both sessions are compulsory and you must clear the minimum qualifying marks in each one separately; missing a session means disqualification. The exact percentages are set in each notification, so read the current one.

faqs.q: What is the educational qualification for MTS and Havaldar?
faqs.a: **Class 10 (matriculation) pass** from a recognised board, with the certificate in hand by the cut-off date in the notification. No graduation is needed.

In the last cycle it was **18-25 years for most MTS posts** and **18-27 years for Havaldar** (and for MTS in selected offices), counted as on 1 August 2025, with relaxations of 3 years for OBC, 5 for SC/ST, 10-15 for PwD and 3 for ex-servicemen after deducting service.

faqs.q: Is there a physical test for MTS?
faqs.a: No. **PET/PST is only for Havaldar** in CBIC and CBN. MTS candidates go from the CBT straight to document verification.

faqs.q: What are the PET standards for Havaldar?
faqs.a: As reported for the last cycle: men walk **1,600 m in 15 minutes** or cycle **8 km in 30 minutes**; women walk **1 km in 20 minutes** or cycle **3 km in 25 minutes**. Physical standards listed are height 157.5 cm and chest 76-81 cm for men, and height 152 cm for women. Confirm against the current notice.

faqs.q: What is the salary of MTS and Havaldar?
faqs.a: Both are **Pay Level 1 (₹18,000-56,900 pay-matrix band)** Group C posts. Your actual take-home depends on the city you are posted in, because DA, HRA and TA are added on top of basic pay.

faqs.q: Is there any interview or Tier 2 in SSC MTS?
faqs.a: No. There is **no interview and no Tier 2**. The selection is the CBT merit (normalised), PET/PST for Havaldar and document verification.

faqs.q: When is the next SSC MTS notification?
faqs.a: It is **not verified yet**. The SSC calendar had planned 30 June 2026, but that date was reportedly postponed and no notice had been confirmed at the time of this update. Watch ssc.gov.in; this page will be updated when the official notice appears.
In the last cycle the fee was **₹100**, with exemption for women, SC, ST, PwBD and ex-servicemen candidates. The next notification will state its own fee.

documents: At Document Verification you typically need: **Class 10 (matriculation) certificate and marksheet** (proof of date of birth and qualification), **category certificate** (OBC/EWS/SC/ST in the central-government format and valid for the relevant year), **PwD or ex-servicemen documents** if you claimed those benefits, a **photo ID** such as Aadhaar, PAN or passport, recent passport photographs, and the print of your application and admit card. Havaldar candidates should also keep their PET/PST admit card and medical or fitness papers handy. Check that your name and date of birth are spelt the same on every document - mismatches cause the most DV delays.
